name: agent-desktop
description: Computer use CLI for AI agents
one_liner: Lets an AI agent see and click through the real buttons and menus of any desktop app on your computer, the way a human would, instead of guessing from a screenshot.
buyer: An automation consultant who gets paid to automate back-office work at companies still running old desktop-only software with no API.
business_use_cases: An RPA shop automates a 15-year-old desktop claims-processing app for a regional insurer that has no exportable API.
A QA team builds an overnight agent that exercises a Windows accounting app end-to-end and reports exactly which screen broke after an update.
A managed-IT provider offers 'AI data entry' as a service, having an agent re-key orders from one legacy desktop system into a newer web app every night.

money_ideas.idea: A per-workflow automation service that builds and maintains agent scripts for a client's specific legacy desktop app.
A hosted API that takes a plain-English instruction plus an app name and returns the verified result of operating that app.

steal_this: Pick one painful, ubiquitous desktop tool (e.g. QuickBooks Desktop) and sell a single automation that exports a nightly report from it, pitched directly to the small businesses still stuck on it.
